rules.sentence: Sleep loss and reduced REM sleep in tauopathies, such as Alzheimer disease, can lead to insomnia and are believed to be due to the degeneration of sleep-promoting regions of the brain.[15]
Impaired amplitude and delayed acrophase of the circadian rhythm in otherwise healthy older individuals increase the risk of developing Alzheimer disease.[16]

A high incidence of both central sleep apnea and OSA is found in patients with Parkinson disease due to the contribution of several factors, such as rigidity, diaphragmatic dyskinesia, stridor, and increased tone in upper airways.[14]
